text:
Charlie McAvoy has nine points and one goal in 14 games, which undersells how well the Bruins play when he is out there. Boston takes 62.7% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice (expected goals measure chance quality), almost 12 points better than without him, and he is doing it in 24 minutes a night against top competition.

The scoring is the soft spot. No goals in his last ten, seven assists, and a points rate below his usual pace; last season he had 61 points. His shooting is at 4.8% on just 21 shots. The Bruins are scoring roughly what their chances deserve with him on the ice, and the assists should follow the possession.

He also matched a franchise legend in the win over Florida, per a Yahoo Sports headline, and his recent words about the Bruins and Canadiens rivalry made the rounds. Evolving-Hockey had him 30th among defensemen last season, a play driver in the 88th percentile. The Bruins have lost their last two badly, 5-2 to Montreal and 6-2 to Minnesota. If they are going to steady, he is the one who drives it from the back.
headline: McAvoy is winning his minutes, quietly
